how: three fresh blind reviewers per round (separate sessions, no access to the code or the answer key): the five levels shuffled and matched to their descriptions; then per level two unlabelled renders (this round and the last, order shuffled) beside the level's photos (L0, L2, L3) or its description (L1, L4). Sheets built from Artifacts/texloop/gelcoat/{before,after}.
against: before (the single ageK material on main)
notes: All three: the ends of the ladder are easy; L1 against L0 is the hardest call (one faint scuff), and the warm cast is what gives L3 away.

All three: the renders are very smooth (no orange peel, little gloss variation), the chalk barely shows, and the rain streaks are too straight and evenly spaced; one called the stacked fender smudges a ladder.
Nobody called it the wrong material, but two said it reads closer to smooth painted plastic than photographed gelcoat.

3.change: 12 cm streak lanes with each run off-centre and wandering as it falls, fewer runs at a given dirt; fender smudge rows staggered
3.why: lost the A/B to round 2 (L2 and L4 read as too clean with fewer runs; L3 was better) and the streaks still read as straight; reverted, so the shipped material is round 2
